title: Show the board the controls

proposed_identity.status: historical precedent only; L13-L16 purpose-specific rights pending

presenter_passages.passage_exact: A Harbor board reviewer asks Morgan a fair question: what happens when the preparation agent produces a brief that looks ready, but the evidence is thin? Morgan brings three paper panels to the table.
Nothing about a clean storyboard lifts the hold.

offscreen_narration.text:
The first panel shows the queue, including held and rejected work. The second follows one item through its trace. The third shows the rule that governed it. This is a design walkthrough, not a live system demonstration. Morgan is showing what Harbor intends to inspect before it trusts the workflow.

Start with the queue. One Session Option Brief is prepared, not proposed to the team. The staffing hold says staffing is unconfirmed. The print request says no spend is approved. The research proposal is not run because its baseline and reviewer protocol are missing. Place the rejections where the reviewer can see them too. A queue that only displays polished outputs hides the decisions that make the operation governable.

Open the trace for the held brief. It begins with cleared Harbor source references. It records the preparation agent's draft, the check that found the staffing gap, the hold, and Morgan as the decision owner. There is no send or booking event. The trace should let someone ask why the item stopped, without exposing raw source notes or pretending a paper receipt is a live audit log. The absence of an event is part of the answer.

Now show memory. Harbor has a proposed local rule: a session cannot move from option to team proposal until a person confirms staffing. In this classroom design, that rule is a draft for Morgan's review. The agent cannot promote it itself, and a single held example cannot become general truth by repetition. Show the rule's owner, scope, source reference, status, and review date. If any are missing, say so.

The workbook asks what export a reviewer can take away. Morgan can offer the scoped proof outline from lesson twelve after a separate audience and privacy review. It would contain the boundary, receipt references, decisions, and limitations. It would omit raw notes and unrelated records. For class today, it stays `not shared`. A reviewer may ask whether the agent actually ran. Answer plainly: no. This exercise demonstrates controls on paper; it does not prove production reliability.

Pause. Which panel would expose the weakest part of your own proposed workflow first?

Storyboard a Three-Panel Demo for your workflow. Give each panel a reviewer question and one piece of evidence. Include a blocked or rejected item beside the successful work. In the trace, name the missing event as clearly as the recorded ones. In memory, identify who may approve the rule. Write two likely skeptical questions and honest answers. Decide what a reviewer may receive, what stays withheld, and who reviews the export before sharing. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data.

Save revision fourteen as a draft. The board can examine Harbor's proposed controls and its unresolved gaps. Morgan still owns the session decision.
